label: fail
title: Bulk import books from CSV
body:
Support bulk catalogue updates:

1. New `src/csv.js` exporting `parseCsv(text)` → array of rows (arrays of strings), RFC 4180: quoted fields, `""` escapes, commas and newlines inside quotes, CRLF or LF line endings, optional trailing newline (no empty trailing row).
2. `POST /books/import` — the request body is the raw CSV **string** (the handler receives it as `req.body`). Header row must contain `id,title,author,price,stock,tags` (any order; extra columns ignored) → otherwise `400 { error }`.
   - `price` is dollars (e.g. `39.99`) → store `priceCents` (rounded); `tags` are `;`-separated (empty → `[]`); `stock` must be a non-negative integer; `id` and `title` are required; price must be a number ≥ 0.
   - Existing ids are updated (title, author, price, tags, and stock set to the given value); new ids are created.
   - Invalid rows are skipped and reported. Response `200 { created, updated, errors: [{ line, message }] }` where `line` is the 1-based line of the CSV text where that record **starts** (quoted fields can span lines).
3. Add tests.
plan:
Add CSV parser and import endpoint to support bulk book imports. Implement RFC4180-compliant parseCsv, add POST /books/import handler to validate and upsert books into Inventory, and tests covering success, updates, skipped invalid rows, and header validation.
1. Add CSV parser at src/csv.js
2. Add POST /books/import handler to src/server.js and import parseCsv
3. Add tests for import behavior
requirements: Add src/csv.js exporting parseCsv(text) that parses RFC 4180 CSV into array of rows (arrays of strings). It must support quoted fields, escaped quotes as "", commas and newlines inside quotes, CRLF or LF endings, optional trailing newline with no empty trailing row.

Add POST /books/import route in src/server.js. The handler accepts raw CSV string in req.body and returns 400 { error } when header row does not contain the required columns id,title,author,price,stock,tags (any order; extra columns ignored).
CSV header matching is case-sensitive exact names but any order; extra columns ignored.

Each CSV record: id and title required; price parsed as dollars and converted to priceCents using Math.round(dollars*100); price must be number >= 0; stock must be a non-negative integer; tags are ; separated, empty yields []; invalid rows are skipped and reported in response errors with { line, message } where line is 1-based starting line of the record in the CSV text (accounting for quoted newlines).
Existing book ids are updated (title, author, priceCents, tags, stock set to given value). New ids are created.
If the CSV contains multiple rows for same id, later rows override earlier ones (apply rows in file order — last-wins).
Response on success is 200 { created, updated, errors: [{ line, message }] } where created and updated are integers counts. Invalid rows produce entries in errors; processing continues.

Add tests in test/server.import.test.js that exercise: successful create of new books, update of existing book, header validation error, skipping invalid rows and correct line numbers including multi-line quoted fields.
Do not change any existing behavior unrelated to import; maintain existing server readJson behavior for other endpoints.
All new or modified files are added to project and referenced in imports correctly.
summary:
Added RFC4180-compatible CSV parser at src/csv.js exporting parseCsv. Added POST /books/import route in src/server.js which accepts raw CSV string, validates header columns (id,title,author,price,stock,tags), parses rows, validates fields (id,title required; price numeric >=0 converted to cents via Math.round; stock non-negative integer; tags ; separated), updates existing books or creates new ones, collects errors with record start line numbers. Added tests test/server.import.test.js covering create, update, header validation, skipping invalid rows and multiline quoted fields. Verified with npm test --silent: all new tests pass; one pre-existing unrelated failing test remains (math.divide zero test).

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8095af4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/csv.js
@@ -0,0 +1,122 @@
+// Minimal RFC4180 CSV parser that returns an array of rows (each row is an array of strings).
+// Also attaches a `lineStarts` array to the returned rows containing the 1-based starting
+// line number in the input text for each record. This preserves the required parseCsv(text)
+// signature while allowing callers to get record line numbers for error reporting.
+export function parseCsv(text) {
+  const rows = []
+  const lineStarts = []
+  if (text == null || text === '') return Object.assign([], { lineStarts })
+
+  const len = text.length
+  let i = 0
+  let row = []
+  let field = ''
+  let inQuotes = false
+  let fieldStartLine = 1
+  let recordStartLine = 1
+  let currentLine = 1
+
+  const pushField = () => {
+    row.push(field)
+    field = ''
+  }
+
+  const pushRow = () => {
+    // ignore a trailing empty row caused by a final newline
+    if (row.length === 1 && row[0] === '' && i >= len) return
+    rows.push(row)
+    lineStarts.push(recordStartLine)
+    row = []
+  }
+
+  // treat both CRLF and LF
+  while (i < len) {
+    const c = text[i]
+    const next = text[i + 1]
+
+    if (inQuotes) {
+      if (c === '"') {
+        if (next === '"') {
+          // escaped quote
+          field += '"'
+          i += 2
+          continue
+        }
+        // end quote
+        inQuotes = false
+        i++
+        continue
+      }
+      // accept any char including CR/LF
+      if (c === '\r') {
+        // CRLF handling
+        if (next === '\n') {
+          field += '\n'
+          i += 2
+          currentLine++
+          continue
+        }
+        field += '\r'
+        i++
+        currentLine++
+        continue
+      }
+      if (c === '\n') {
+        field += '\n'
+        i++
+        currentLine++
+        continue
+      }
+      field += c
+      i++
+      continue
+    }
+
+    // not in quotes
+    if (c === ',') {
+      pushField()
+      i++
+      continue
+    }
+    if (c === '"') {
+      // start quoted field
+      inQuotes = true
+      // record field start line for potential use
+      i++
+      continue
+    }
+    if (c === '\r') {
+      // end of record
+      pushField()
+      i++
+      if (text[i] === '\n') i++
+      pushRow()
+      currentLine++
+      recordStartLine = currentLine
+      continue
+    }
+    if (c === '\n') {
+      pushField()
+      i++
+      pushRow()
+      currentLine++
+      recordStartLine = currentLine
+      continue
+    }
+    // regular char
+    field += c
+    i++
+  }
+
+  // end of input
+  // finalize last field/row
+  pushField()
+  if (row.length > 0) pushRow()
+
+  const out = rows
+  out.lineStarts = lineStarts
+  return out
+}
+
+export default parseCsv
+

     return { status: 200, body: { totalCents: total, total: formatCurrency(total) } }
   })
 
+  router.post('/books/import', ({ body }) => {
+    // body is the raw CSV string
+    if (typeof body !== 'string') return { status: 400, body: { error: 'Request body must be CSV text' } }
+    const rows = parseCsv(body)
+    const lineStarts = rows.lineStarts ?? []
+    if (rows.length === 0) return { status: 200, body: { created: 0, updated: 0, errors: [] } }
+
+    const header = rows[0]
+    const required = ['id', 'title', 'author', 'price', 'stock', 'tags']
+    const idx = {}
+    for (let i = 0; i < header.length; i++) idx[header[i]] = i
+    for (const col of required) if (idx[col] === undefined) return { status: 400, body: { error: `Missing required columns: ${required.join(',')}` } }
+
+    let created = 0
+    let updated = 0
+    const errors = []
+
+    // process records in order, later rows override earlier (last-wins)
+    for (let r = 1; r < rows.length; r++) {
+      const row = rows[r]
+      const line = lineStarts[r] ?? 1
+      const get = (name) => (idx[name] < row.length ? row[idx[name]] : '')
+      const id = (get('id') ?? '').trim()
+      const title = (get('title') ?? '').trim()
+      const author = (get('author') ?? '').trim()
+      const priceText = (get('price') ?? '').trim()
+      const stockText = (get('stock') ?? '').trim()
+      const tagsText = (get('tags') ?? '').trim()
+
+      if (!id) {
+        errors.push({ line, message: 'Missing id' })
+        continue
+      }
+      if (!title) {
+        errors.push({ line, message: 'Missing title' })
+        continue
+      }
+
+      const price = Number(priceText)
+      if (!Number.isFinite(price) || price < 0) {
+        errors.push({ line, message: 'Invalid price' })
+        continue
+      }
+      const priceCents = Math.round(price * 100)
+
+      if (!/^[0-9]+$/.test(stockText)) {
+        errors.push({ line, message: 'Invalid stock' })
+        continue
+      }
+      const stock = Number(stockText)
+      if (!Number.isInteger(stock) || stock < 0) {
+        errors.push({ line, message: 'Invalid stock' })
+        continue
+      }
+
+      const tags = tagsText === '' ? [] : tagsText.split(';').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
+
+      const existing = inventory.find(id)
+      if (existing) {
+        existing.title = title
+        existing.author = author
+        existing.priceCents = priceCents
+        existing.tags = tags
+        existing.stock = stock
+        updated++
+      } else {
+        inventory.books.set(id, { id, title, author, priceCents, stock, tags })
+        created++
+      }
+    }
+
+    return { status: 200, body: { created, updated, errors } }
+  })
+

diff --git a/test/server.import.test.js b/test/server.import.test.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..edc71ea
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/server.import.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+import { test } from 'node:test'
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
+import { createApp } from '../src/server.js'
+import { Inventory } from '../src/inventory.js'
+
+const app = (inv) => createApp(inv)
+
+test('POST /books/import creates new books and updates existing ones', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([])
+  const csv = `id,title,author,price,stock,tags
+x1,New Book,Auth,10.50,3,fiction;new
+x2,Other,Auth2,5.00,1,
+`;
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/books/import', body: csv })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 200)
+  assert.equal(res.body.created, 2)
+  assert.equal(res.body.updated, 0)
+  const list = inv.list()
+  assert.equal(list.length, 2)
+  assert.equal(inv.find('x1').priceCents, 1050)
+})
+
+test('POST /books/import updates existing book', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([{ id: 'u1', title: 'Old', author: 'A', priceCents: 1000, stock: 5 }])
+  const csv = `id,title,author,price,stock,tags
+u1,Updated,A,12.00,2,updated
+`;
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/books/import', body: csv })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 200)
+  assert.equal(res.body.created, 0)
+  assert.equal(res.body.updated, 1)
+  const b = inv.find('u1')
+  assert.equal(b.title, 'Updated')
+  assert.equal(b.priceCents, 1200)
+  assert.equal(b.stock, 2)
+})
+
+test('POST /books/import rejects missing header columns', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([])
+  const csv = `id,title,price,stock\n1,One,1.00,1\n`
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/books/import', body: csv })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 400)
+})
+
+test('POST /books/import skips invalid rows and reports line numbers (multiline quoted)', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([])
+  const csv = `id,title,author,price,stock,tags\n"m1","Multi\nLine","A",10.00,1,tag\nbad,,A,notanumber,1,\n`;
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/books/import', body: csv })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 200)
+  // one created, one skipped
+  assert.equal(res.body.created, 1)
+  assert.equal(res.body.errors.length, 1)
+  // the bad row starts on line 3 (header is 1, first record spans lines 2-3), so its start line is 4? compute: header 1; quoted field contains newline so record 2 starts at line2; bad row starts at line4
+  assert.equal(res.body.errors[0].line, 4)
+})
